location.mountain: Yiwu Mountain (one of the Six Famous Tea Mountains)

characteristics.cultivar: Old-tree Camellia sinensis var. assamica (gu shu), aged 50 to 500+ years
characteristics.oxidation: Minimal at production; undergoes slow post-fermentation during storage

description.short: Compressed tea from Yiwu arbor trees, naturally aged without artificial fermentation and evolving over decades
description.overview: Yiwu is one of the most revered pu-erh regions, celebrated for its gentle yet deep and sweet sheng pu-erh crafted from arbor trees of various ages, including ancient tea trees.
description.leaf: Large, gently twisted dark-green leaves; compressed into a dense cake (bingcha)
description.liquor: Ranges from pale yellow (young tea) to amber and deep honey (aged tea)
description.aroma: Floral, honeyed, with dried fruit notes; developing woody and earthy nuances with age
description.taste: When young: fresh, slightly astringent, with pleasant bitterness quickly transforming into sweetness (hui gan); with age: mellow, deep, and sweet
description.aftertaste: Long-lasting sweet finish in the throat, strong "cha qi" — a sensation of warmth and vitality typical of ancient trees
description.processing: Plucking → withering → pan fixation (shaqing) at lower temperatures to preserve enzymes → rolling → sun-drying (maocha) → steam compression into cakes → natural aging

history.origin: Yiwu was a primary gathering center along the legendary Ancient Tea Horse Road (Cha Ma Gu Dao), from which compressed tea was carried to Tibet and neighboring regions
history.development: In the 19th century, Yiwu was the epicenter of the pu-erh trade, home to renowned private tea houses (hao) whose vintage cakes are now legendary collector's items
history.modern: After decades of quiet in the 20th century, enthusiasm for Yiwu rebounded in the 1990s and 2000s as collectors sought out the superior qualities of its ancient arbor trees
interestingFacts: Ancient tea trees in the forests surrounding Yiwu are estimated to be several hundred years old
Authentic sheng pu-erh can age and improve for decades; well-preserved cakes from the 1990s command prices comparable to precious artifacts
